21 major banks plan joint USD stablecoin –
Link
A coalition of 21 financial institutions plans to form a company this year and launch a dollar-pegged stablecoin in H1 2027, with a euro token to follow. The group includes Goldman Sachs, BofA, Citi, and Deutsche Bank.
Matters because: this points to accelerating bank-led entry into blockchain-based settlement, even if adoption still lags incumbents like Tether.

Solana processed 5B transactions in August; Alpenglow upgrade set for October –
Link
Solana disclosed it processed 5 billion transactions in August, more than all other blockchains combined. It also confirmed its Alpenglow upgrade is slated for October.
Alpenglow is expected to cut confirmation times from ≈12 seconds to ≈400ms.
Matters because: Continued high usage supports Solana's competitive positioning versus other L1s, and the upgrade could strengthen that case if it ships on schedule.

Crypto profits come from riding positive volume delta - the expansion of attention and trading activity, either internally (existing traders rotating into a new narrative) or externally (new participants entering) - before volume saturates and the delta turns negative, after which price typically follows down, as seen in SOL’s delayed blow-off versus BERA’s day-one peak-and-fade
This cycle’s external volume delta is historically weak, with no large new cohort of traders arriving to rescue late holders, so altcoin market-cap ceilings keep compressing (Doge $80B → Trump/Pepe ~$10B) while BTC stays the exception because it still attracts recurring volume and walks its cost basis higher
TLDR: careful that you don't dream too high for your on-chain bags, $50m mc coins alr get people euphoric this cycle
